title: Banks completion tools resolve untrusted import paths into executable callables
summary: Banks through 2.4.2 parses tool definitions from completion bodies and resolves their import_path without an allowlist. A matching model tool call can invoke an attacker-selected Python callable with attacker-controlled arguments.

severity.rationale: Code execution requires attacker influence over a completion body and a matching tool call. These conditions can arise in agents using shared or network-supplied prompts, so the tool boundary warrants prompt patching.

affected.note: Affected through 2.4.2. The separate Jinja sandbox fix in 2.4.2 does not fix this issue.

exposure: Requires attacker-influenced completion content and an LLM that emits tool calls. Execution inherits the Banks process privileges.

remediation.details: Upgrade to 2.4.3 or later. The fix resolves callables from an explicit tool registry instead of arbitrary imports.
remediation.risk: Medium. Applications may need to adapt tool registration; validate trusted completion flows.

verification: Confirm the resolved Banks package is patched and completion tools use explicit registration.

review.notes: Independent reviewer re-read every tier 1 source and checked every field. No open findings.

history.change: Initial record drafted for independent review.
